analysis_notes.torah_structure: LM2 Torah 38 is a 7-paragraph teaching about the relationship between the Tzaddik and his students. Its argument: (1) Sometimes the great one must go to the small one — this itself marks a supremely high level. (2) Moshe's humility illustrates this: 'wherever you find his greatness, there you find his humility.' (3) The central act is transforming מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת → מֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת (contracted → expanded consciousness), which IS the המתקה (sweetening) — the one bechina in the dataset. (4) This transformation is achieved via two methods: הֶאָרַת פָּנִים (radiant face) or יִסּוּרִין (suffering/affliction). (5) The self-nullification of the great one during this process is not a loss — it is temporary and results in the student's complete elevation. (6) The degree of closeness required depends on the student's state, illustrated by the candle analogy: a partially-extinguished candle (with some light remaining) only needs to be brought close, while a completely extinguished one must be brought directly to the flame (or vice versa).
